title: Dreaming-state-record (predicating-regime fiber state; ω < κ < ω₁)
description: Regime: transfinite-predication-category (predicating-regime fiber state record). Derivation from the four-regime grammar in CLAUDE.md: the state record describes a predication-fiber's condition (sensory predicates → ⊥, internal composition continues). Predication-fibers and their states live in the transfinite-predication-category (κ < ω₁). Operational definition (independently derived, not citing lab as authority — the lab note happens to describe the same operational pattern): a dreaming entity has its sensory predicates disconnected from environment — respond(dreamer, environment) = ⊥ — while internal predicates continue composing — respond(dreamer-internal, dreamer-memories) ≠ ⊥. The state record exists at platform scope (AOP/library/) because it's metadata about AOP-level agents; its REGIME is predicating because what it describes is a fiber-state. Cross-regime composition with tick: when a tick (settling-regime, κ < ω) acts on an entity carrying a dreaming-state-record, the closure-rule set used is RESTRICTED — sensory rules evaluate to ⊥. The tick remains settling-regime; the predicating-regime state prunes its rule-set. EXPLICIT NON-EQUIVALENCE with OpenClaw's 'LLM dreaming' pattern: OpenClaw uses LLM passes to consolidate memory between sessions — that would be an aperiodic-articulating act (LLM call = articulating). Our dreaming is NOT that — we run settling on the pruned rule-set; no inferring morphism is invoked during a dream-tick.
